maya (support): Heads-up — customer SUP-8321 reporting mid-stream cut: client gets partial output then connection closes. Happening on mobile app during WiFi<>cell flip. Attached client log snippet below. Can we triage?

james (sre): Thanks. Can you paste the request_id / conn id + model + approx token count? Any server_request_id header from the client logs?

maya (support): request_id=rc_7a1f2b, conn_id=stream-3321, model=redwood-large, approx tokens ~1200. Client log shows: 
```
[2026-02-18T14:22:11.123Z] SSE: connected
[2026-02-18T14:22:24.987Z] SSE: received data chunk (partial)
[2026-02-18T14:22:29.004Z] HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
[2026-02-18T14:22:29.005Z] SSE: connection closed by server
```
Customer says this happens reliably when phone switches from corporate WiFi -> LTE.

elena (eng-runtime): That pattern smells like a token rotation race: short-lived client token expires while client loses network, refresh happens, reconnect attempt has different token but server sees a transient 401 and tears down the stream. Two quick questions: 1) are you using short session tokens (TTL <= 60s)? 2) does the client try to reconnect automatically, or does it expect the server to resume?

maya (support): They use a 60s session token via our SDK. Client tries to reconnect once with new token. They expect to resume the same conversation (conversation_id param).

james (sre): Also consider NAT timeouts/proxy reassign on carrier handoff. If the client loses TCP and later reconnects with a new 5-tuple, the server treats it as new connection. If token expired during that gap, server rejects. Two mitigations: increase token refresh buffer client-side (refresh 15s before expiry) and enable client keepalive pings to keep NAT mapping during short handoffs.

elena (eng-runtime): Agreed. Quick workaround for SUP-8321: increase client-side refresh window to 15-20s and make reconnect logic retry on 401 with exponential backoff while passing conversation_id so the server can attach new stream to the existing session if possible. Long term: we should support a short auth grace window server-side (5-10s) to accept a recently-expired token for stream reconnection, or return an SSE comment line with an explicit `event: auth_expired` instead of hard close so clients can react gracefully.

maya (support): Repro steps I gave customer: 1) set token TTL=60s, 2) start stream on WiFi, 3) force network switch to LTE, 4) observe 401 and stream close ~within 4-8s. They included a packet capture showing SYN from new IP then 401.

james (sre): Pasted the relevant server side log for request_id=rc_7a1f2b: 
```
[2026-02-18T14:22:28.999Z] conn=stream-3321 request_id=rc_7a1f2b auth_check=failed reason=token_expired
[2026-02-18T14:22:29.001Z] conn=stream-3321 stream=terminated code=401
```
We don't currently have a resume flow for SSE streams when auth fails mid-stream.

elena (eng-runtime): For immediate mitigation I can push a small client-facing doc + example code showing: 1) send periodic SSE comment keepalive lines from client to keep NAT; 2) refresh token earlier; 3) on 401, automatically retry reconnect with new token and conversation_id. Example keepalive client snippet: 
```js
// send every 15s while streaming to avoid NAT
fetch(streamUrl, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } })
// on open: setInterval(() => {
//   source.dispatchEvent(new MessageEvent('message', { data: ':keepalive\n\n' }));
// }, 15000)
```
(We know browsers can only send via fetch/ws; mobile native can POST a small heartbeat to keep the mapping).

deploy-bot: Note: created follow-up ticket ENG-RT-559 to evaluate server-side grace window for token rotation.

maya (support): I'll send the workaround + snippet to the customer and ask them to try the refresh buffer + reconnect-on-401 approach. Tagging eng-runtime to keep ENG-RT-559 prioritized for a resilience fix. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
